summary: Explains dynamic role reuse with `include_role`, which runs in task order rather than before tasks. Vars and tags can be passed; a tag applies only to the include itself, so `--tags` only selects role tasks with the same tag. Roles can be included conditionally with `when`.
questions: How do I run a role in the middle of my tasks?
What's the difference between roles: and include_role in when the role runs?
Why doesn't tagging include_role tag the tasks inside the role?
How do I include a role only on RedHat hosts?
Can I pass vars to include_role?

answer_card.title: Include roles dynamically
answer_card.answer_md:
`include_role` runs the role where it appears in `tasks` (roles in `roles:` run before all tasks):
```yaml
- hosts: webservers
  tasks:
    - ansible.builtin.debug: {msg: "before the role"}
    - ansible.builtin.include_role:
        name: example
    - ansible.builtin.debug: {msg: "after the role"}
```
Pass vars and tags:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.include_role:
    name: foo_app_instance
  vars:
    dir: '/opt/a'
    app_port: 5000
  tags: typeA
```
A tag on `include_role` applies **only** to the include itself; `--tags` will run only role tasks that carry the same tag.

Conditionally:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.include_role:
    name: some_role
  when: "ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'RedHat'"
```
